claim: OpenAI introduced beta next-message composer predictions in Codex on October 9, 2026, with explicit user acceptance before sending.
verifiedFacts: OpenAI's October 9 release notes describe beta composer predictions in Codex desktop threads, with Tab to accept a proposed next message.
The release notes say accepting a prediction does not send it automatically and the beta is restricted to eligible Pro users on supported local or SSH threads.
inference: Predictive agent instructions may reduce friction but can also bias investigation; preserve deliberate human approval and prompt-diff visibility.
Consultancy implication: Use as a UX research reference for consentful AI suggestions and decision provenance.
Project disposition implication: design-standards CORE for interaction guidance; seed-loom CORE for explicit approval boundaries.
significance: A small interface change creates a useful test of anticipatory assistance versus reasoning autonomy.
assumptions: Suggested next actions measurably improve developer productivity without narrowing exploration.
knownLimitations: Beta availability is limited; no independent productivity or cognitive-bias study inspected.
Not evidence of autonomous agent task execution.
